name: EFC Atlas - external evidence subgraph
description: Typed, provenance-preserving links from independent external results to existing Atlas phenomena and existing regime-node ids, at the lowest justified epistemic strength. Nothing in this file may raise an external result above candidate compatibility, and nothing in it settles an EFC prediction. The sealed prediction cards (atlas.json tier1_demo_predictions) are the only place a prediction status lives.

policy.ceiling_definition: The strongest link this register may carry is candidate compatibility: the external result does not contradict the EFC regime expectation, and does not test it. No link in this file is evidence FOR EFC, and no link is a settlement.
policy.attribution_rule: An external author's interpretation is recorded as the author's interpretation. Where the author names an unknown process, this file records an unknown process - never an EFC mechanism. EFC attribution is only written where an EFC-sealed document states the expectation, and then with its DOI.
policy.settlement_rule: A prediction is settled only by an identity-matched settlement message on the prediction bus, or by the named arbiter publishing the measurement. A paper that is adjacent to the arbiter is not the arbiter. A pending contract stays pending here.

link_types.definition: The external result does not contradict the EFC regime expectation for the same observable, at the stated scale.
may_not_be_read_as: evidence that the EFC mechanism is the cause

link_types.definition: A competing mechanism - theoretical or astrophysical - that could produce the same observable without EFC.
A result that, if it holds, weakens the premise that the observable is anomalous and therefore the reason EFC was invoked there.
may_not_be_read_as: an established result (this one is conditional in its own source)

link_types.definition: An independent measurement of the same parameter, carrying its own uncertainty and its own systematic budget, which bounds an EFC point value without testing the mechanism.
may_not_be_read_as: a bracket of the EFC value where the arithmetic does not bracket it

link_types.definition: An inference whose effect on an EFC-relevant quantity depends on a stated condition that the source itself marks as conditional.
may_not_be_read_as: a measurement at the redshift the EFC claim is about

fragments.title: Candidate sign reversal of the ISW effect in local voids (z<0.03)
fragments.observed: A significant CMB temperature excess in the direction of local underdensities within z<0.03, growing with void size and reaching about 3.5 sigma for the largest voids; fewer than 0.2 percent of simulated CMB maps show a similarly significant excess. Combined with earlier cooling of CMB photons in nearby filaments (>5 sigma at z<0.02), the authors read this as possible evidence for a negative ISW effect locally. Removing the quadrupole, the mean void-versus-galaxy temperature difference is almost 6.5 sigma larger than in simulations. The observed amplitude is an order of magnitude larger than the predicted Rees-Sciama and ISW effects.
fragments.observer_instrument: Planck SMICA CMB maps crossed with void catalogues built by the Sparkling and Revolver finders; 10 000 SMICA simulations for the null distribution (1000 for the standard deviations); quadrupole estimated outside the Planck common mask and removed from data and simulations alike.
fragments.redshift_or_scale: z<0.03; median void radius about 10 degrees (typically R_void > 13 Mpc; largest quartile R_void > 17 Mpc); 69 +/- 4 open voids, 110 +/- 3 in the volume-limited sample.
model_assumptions: Voids are identified by two finder algorithms; the authors correct explicitly for the choice of sample, wavelet scale (3, 4, 5 degrees) and the fraction of the void radius used.
The RS/ISW expectation is computed in LambdaCDM; the anomaly is defined as a deviation from that expectation.

The quadrupole (about 5 percent of the anticorrelation) is removed to break the void-galaxy anticorrelation; the authors state the residual anticorrelation is 2-5 percent depending on the void sample.
limitations: The authors' own interpretation is an unknown physical process, possibly a non-standard model of dark energy - not EFC and not any named mechanism.
The look-elsewhere effect is corrected for, but the detection is a local (z<0.03) sample with modest void statistics.

The amplitude is an order of magnitude larger than the predicted RS/ISW terms. EFC's void sign-flip is a Rees-Sciama-type term, so the amplitude is a live problem for that mechanism too unless dmu/drho yields a much larger term - which the EFC package summary read here does not show.
Independent confirmation is claimed from Davies et al. (2025) using cosmic tunnels; that paper was not read in this pass and is recorded as the authors' reference, not as verified.

links.rationale: The sign reported here (hot voids, cold overdensities) is the same sign EFC's sealed void-ISW prediction requires for deep voids (theory DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.31942677; pipeline DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.31990212). The match is a sign match in a local void sample, not a test: the EFC prediction is depth-binned with a turnover near delta ~ -0.8 and an amplification requirement at R_v > 100 h^-1 Mpc, and this paper bins by void size and radius, not by the EFC depth coordinate.
does_not_imply: that EFC causes the observed excess
that the EFC void sign-flip prediction has been observed
that the amplitude agrees - the observed amplitude is an order of magnitude above the standard RS/ISW terms

links.rationale: The observation node obs.isw is the regime-node registry's reading of the ISW cross-correlation; this fragment is one measurement feeding that node's band, not a new node and not a new predicate.
does_not_imply: that this changes obs.isw's evidence status
that this promotes the node beyond proxy evidence

fragments.discriminator: Depth-binned void-CMB stacking with the EFC coordinate (A_ISW versus delta, expecting a turnover near delta ~ -0.8) and a radius trend at R_v > 100 h^-1 Mpc. If the hot-void signal persists at shallow depths and shows no depth turnover, EFC's P1 mechanism is not what is being seen; if it appears only in deep voids with the predicted sign, the candidate compatibility becomes a real test.

fragments.title: GR peculiar-velocity flux as an alternative growth mechanism (delta proportional to t)
fragments.observed: A theoretical result within general relativity: the purely relativistic contribution of peculiar-velocity flux to the gravitational field adds a mode to the linear density evolution, raising the growth rate from delta proportional to t^(2/3) to delta proportional to t, and the present density contrast from about 1e-2 to about 1e-0.5. The stated aim is to accommodate massive early galaxies without new physics or fine-tuning.
fragments.observer_instrument: No instrument: this is an analytic derivation in a Friedmann model, presented as a Gravity Research Foundation essay.
fragments.redshift_or_scale: Post-recombination dust era; the enhancement is a background-relativistic effect, not gated to a particular z window by construction.
model_assumptions: Standard general relativity and standard Friedmann cosmology, with no new fields or species.
The relativistic growth rate for linear peculiar velocities (v proportional to t^(4/3)) is taken from prior work and inserted into the density evolution equation.
The peculiar-flux term is retained in the energy-momentum tensor and in the relativistic conservation laws.
limitations: Model-derived theory. No data comparison, no fitted amplitude, no error budget in the essay read.
The essay does not state at what scale or redshift the enhancement saturates, nor how it avoids overproducing low-redshift growth - the natural counter-check against sigma8.
It is presented as an alternative to new-physics solutions; it is a rival explanation, not a measurement.

links.rationale: EFC addresses the same phenomenon with a regime-gated early boost (atlas addressing EFC -> early_structure_JWST, mechanism S_flow_boost_at_high_z). Tsagas offers a GR-only route to the same observable. Recording both is the point of the Atlas: two mechanisms, one observable, no arbitration yet.
does_not_imply: that Tsagas refutes EFC
that EFC and Tsagas are the same mechanism
that either explains the JWST sample

links.rationale: A growth rate of delta proportional to t after recombination is an enhancement of the linear growth amplitude at all z, which is the same quantity the fsigma8 node measures at z ~ 0.7. If the mechanism were real and unsuppressed, it would push the growth amplitude ABOVE LambdaCDM - the opposite direction from EFC's mu<1 damping - so the two mechanisms are separable in principle, not merely rival labels.
does_not_imply: that the enhancement is observed
a change to the fsigma8 measurement band

fragments.discriminator: The sign of the growth offset relative to LambdaCDM and its redshift dependence. Tsagas's term is not regime-gated: it should raise the growth amplitude broadly, including at the CMB-era amplitude normalisation. EFC's is gated to the L1->L2 transition and damped (mu<1). A measured fsigma8 offset that is high at all z favours the peculiar-flux class; one that appears only late and downward favours the EFC direction. DESI DR2 full-shape RSD is the named arbiter for the EFC side; nothing here settles the Tsagas side.

fragments.title: Bottom-heavy IMF as a conditional mass correction for possible early progenitors
fragments.observed: From ultra-deep spectra of nine massive quiescent galaxies at z ~ 0.7 (JWST IMFERNO NIRSpec extended with VLT LEGA-C), the most massive galaxies show an excess of low-mass stars, and the oldest galaxy (formation redshift z_form > 5) has the most bottom-heavy IMF. The authors state this galaxy may be a descendant of JWST's 'impossibly early' galaxies, implying those progenitors may have had similarly bottom-heavy IMFs, increasing their masses by a factor of approximately 4 +/- 1.
fragments.observer_instrument: JWST NIRSpec (IMFERNO programme) plus VLT LEGA-C spectra, fitted with full-spectrum stellar-population models (ALF).
fragments.redshift_or_scale: The measurement is at z ~ 0.7 (nine galaxies; oldest with z_form > 5). The factor ~4 +/- 1 is an inference about possible progenitors at higher z, not a measurement at z > 10.
model_assumptions: The low-mass IMF is inferred from an extrapolation of the Milky Way IMF shape in the full-spectrum fit; the authors state that the low-mass contribution is not directly observed.
IMF mismatch is translated into a mass correction via the fitted stellar-population model.
The progenitor link is by descent: the z ~ 0.7 remnant is assumed to be a descendant of an early massive galaxy.
limitations: Nine galaxies at z ~ 0.7. Not a z > 10 sample and not a direct high-redshift mass measurement.
The ~4 +/- 1 factor is conditional in the source ('may', 'implying'), and it applies to possible progenitors, not to the observed galaxies.
It does not measure the IMF at z > 10; it removes a systematic in the mass estimate for a subset if the progenitor assumption holds.
The source's own framing is that the finding may amplify the tension with galaxy-formation models, not that it resolves it.

links.rationale: If early-galaxy stellar masses are systematically underestimated by a factor of a few because of IMF variation, then the premise that the JWST sample requires new cosmological growth physics is weakened - and EFC's S_flow boost at high z is one of the mechanisms invoked on that premise. This is recorded as a conditional defeater of the premise, not as a refutation of EFC.
does_not_imply: that EFC's early-structure addressing is refuted
that the factor 4 applies to z > 10 objects
that the IMF correction is established

fragments.discriminator: A z > 10 IMF measurement (spectroscopic, not extrapolated) or a progenitor test that does not assume descent: dynamical versus stellar masses at high z, and whether the required mass correction scales with the same IMF mismatch parameter measured at z ~ 0.7. If the correction is confirmed at z > 10, the anomaly budget shrinks and EFC's early-boost addressing loses its motivation; if the mismatch does not extend, the anomaly stands.

fragments.title: KiDS-Legacy cosmic shear: S8 = 0.815 (+0.016/-0.021), 0.73 sigma from Planck
fragments.observed: S8 = sigma8 sqrt(Omega_m/0.3) = 0.815 (+0.016/-0.021), in agreement at 0.73 sigma with the Planck Legacy CMB result. Sigma8 = 0.821 (+0.014/-0.016) with alpha = 0.58. 1347 square degrees, lensed sample to z_B <= 2.0, about 32 percent improvement in constraining power over previous KiDS.
fragments.observer_instrument: Kilo-Degree Survey nine-band imaging (1347 sq deg) plus 23 sq deg of KiDS-like calibration spectroscopy; cosmic shear two-point functions with a halo-mass and spectral-type dependent intrinsic-alignment model and marginalisation over baryon feedback.
fragments.redshift_or_scale: Photometric redshift z_B <= 2.0; angular scales of the shear two-point analysis; S8 defined at z = 0.
model_assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM for the headline S8 (the paper also reports Sigma8 with an optimised alpha).
The intrinsic-alignment model is physically motivated but is itself a model choice.
Baryon feedback on the non-linear power spectrum is marginalised, not measured.
limitations: A single survey's 3x2pt-equivalent shear analysis; the paper reports internal and external consistency tests in a companion paper (Stolzner et al.), which was not read here.

The increase in S8 relative to previous KiDS is attributed by the authors to improved redshift distribution estimation and calibration - that is, to a change in the analysis chain, which is exactly the kind of shift that makes cross-survey comparison fragile.
It measures S8; it does not test a growth mechanism, so it cannot distinguish EFC's Sigma<1 from other low-or-central S8 models.

links.rationale: An independent shear measurement of the same parameter EFC's P4 addresses. Its central value (0.815) sits 0.005 below the EFC point value 0.82, and its 1-sigma upper edge (0.831) reaches 0.82. That is a looser relation than 'brackets from above' and does not test the mechanism.
does_not_imply: a pass of P4
that the EFC value is confirmed
that S8 is resolved

links.rationale: P4's falsifier F4 is a Rubin LSST DP2 + Euclid DR1 combined measurement consistent with Planck at <1 sigma; KiDS-Legacy is neither of those datasets and its 0.73-sigma Planck agreement is a different statement. It constrains the same number without discharging the falsifier.
does_not_imply: that F4 has fired
that the P4 badge should change

fragments.discriminator: The named arbiter (Rubin LSST DP2 + Euclid DR1 combined). Between now and then, the discriminating question is whether the DES Y6 / KiDS-Legacy split survives a common analysis chain: if the two surveys converge under a shared pipeline, the 'heterogeneous newest results' reading loses force; if they do not, the split itself is the observable and no single S8 value should be used as the comparison point.

fragments.title: DES Y6 3x2pt: S8 = 0.789 +/- 0.012, 2.6 sigma projected difference from CMB
fragments.observed: S8 = sigma8 (Omega_m/0.3)^0.5 = 0.789 +/- 0.012 and Omega_m = 0.333 (+0.023/-0.028) in flat LambdaCDM. The full-space parameter difference from Planck 2018 + ACT-DR6 + SPT-3G DR1 is 1.8 sigma; projected into S8 alone it is 2.6 sigma. In wCDM, S8 = 0.782 (+0.021/-0.020) and w = -1.12 (+0.26/-0.20).
fragments.observer_instrument: Dark Energy Survey six-year 3x2pt: cosmic shear from 140 million source galaxy shapes, clustering of 9 million lens galaxies, and galaxy-galaxy lensing over about 5000 square degrees.
fragments.redshift_or_scale: DES Y6 footprint, lens and source redshift distributions as calibrated by the collaboration; S8 defined at z = 0.
model_assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM for the headline value, with wCDM reported separately.
The 2.6-sigma figure is a projection of a multi-parameter difference onto S8 alone; the full-space difference is 1.8 sigma. The two numbers answer different questions.
Intrinsic alignment and baryonic feedback are modelled and marginalised within the collaboration's pipeline.
limitations: A single collaboration's pipeline. The paper's own framing is that the tension is with a COMBINED CMB baseline (Planck + ACT-DR6 + SPT-3G), not with Planck alone.
The 2.6-sigma projection is not a measurement of EFC or against it; it is a statement about LambdaCDM parameter consistency across probes.
Using this value as one endpoint of a 'bracket' around 0.82 is arithmetically wrong: 0.789 is 2.58 sigma below 0.82 and its 1-sigma interval [0.777, 0.801] does not contain 0.82.

links.rationale: The lowest of the current survey central values and the one that makes 'S8 ~ 0.82 is bracketed' numerically false. Recorded as a constraint with its own baseline (combined CMB), not as a low-S8 confirmation of EFC.
does_not_imply: that EFC's predicted suppression is measured
that the EFC value 0.82 is excluded
that DES Y6 and KiDS-Legacy can be averaged into one number

links.rationale: P4's point value 0.82 is 2.58 sigma above this central value using the paper's own uncertainty. That is a real, quantified relation between an EFC point value and the newest survey - and it belongs to the record whether or not it flatters the prediction.
does_not_imply: that this kills P4
that this passes P4

fragments.discriminator: A common-pipeline reanalysis of DES Y6 and KiDS-Legacy, and the P4 arbiter (Rubin LSST DP2 + Euclid DR1). Until then the honest statement is that the two newest shear surveys differ from each other by more than either differs from the EFC point value.

fragments.title: EFC's own Planck test: no preference for EFC-type modifications; LambdaCDM best in the CMB regime
fragments.observed: Two channels were tested against Planck 2018 with CLASS and chi-squared statistics: a microphysical photon-baryon coupling modification and a background H(z) modification. The author's stated result is that, done correctly, the CMB data show no preference for any EFC-type modification and that standard LambdaCDM remains the best description of the microwave background.
fragments.observer_instrument: Planck 2018 likelihoods (plik_lite TTTEEE + lowl + lensing), modified CLASS, parameter sweeps and two-dimensional fits.
fragments.redshift_or_scale: The CMB epoch (recombination and the acoustic peaks); the L0/L1 regime in EFC's own labelling.
model_assumptions: The EFC-type modifications tested are the two named channels (photon-baryon coupling; background gate).
The null is interpreted against EFC-R's expectation that the CMB epoch is the regime where EFC effects should be weakest.
limitations: This is a null result. It is not evidence for EFC in any direction, and the author's reframing ('in reality, it is the opposite') is an expectation-based reading, not a measurement.
It constrains the two tested channels; it does not constrain the perturbation-sector channels (mu, Sigma, eta) that EFC's later claims rely on.
Same author as the framework: recorded as an internal result, not independent validation.

links.rationale: The null bounds the background and photon-baryon channels at the acoustic-peak epoch. It is placed here so the Atlas cannot later cite the CMB regime as positive support.
does_not_imply: positive evidence for EFC
that the perturbation sector is constrained
that the L0 recovery is a success rather than a design property

fragments.discriminator: A perturbation-sector (mu, Sigma) fit to the same Planck likelihoods with a reported delta-chi-squared, which does not yet exist as a public EFC result at the precision needed. Until then the L0 recovery is a consistency property, and the null stays a null.

guards.quote: The final result was clear: when the analysis is done correctly, the CMB data show no preference for any EFC-type modification. Standard ΛCDM remains the best description of the microwave background.
guards.why_it_is_not_evidence: The page continues 'At first glance this might appear to be a negative result for EFC. In reality, it is the opposite.' That move converts a null into support by appealing to a pre-registered expectation about which regime EFC should be weakest in. An expectation met by a null is a consistency property; it is not a measurement of the mechanism, and it cannot be counted as positive evidence.
guards.rule: No page, card or ledger entry may cite the CMB null as support for EFC. It may be cited as (a) a bound on the two tested channels and (b) a consistency check of the regime story. Wording: 'no preference / LambdaCDM best in that regime', never 'confirmed the regime structure'.

guards.quote: DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints
guards.why_it_is_not_evidence: The P2 arbiter is DESI DR2 FULL-SHAPE RSD fsigma8 at z ~ 0.7. This paper is the BAO companion. Citing a same-release companion paper as the arbiter makes a pending contract look settled.
guards.rule: Before any statement that a prediction's arbiter has returned, name the paper that reports the arbiter quantity itself, and quote its number. Release-name adjacency (same survey, same data release) is not identity.

guards.why_it_is_not_evidence: Two surveys whose central values multiply rather than bracket a third number, and which disagree with each other by more than either disagrees with the EFC point value, cannot be used as the two ends of an interval around that point value. The 'bracket' language did that arithmetic implicitly and got it wrong.
guards.rule: When comparing a prediction to two surveys, state each central value with its uncertainty and the distance to the prediction in sigma. Never write 'bracketed by' unless the prediction lies inside the interval named.

The prediction bus was read live on 2026-11-12 (prediction subject, state subject, and stream inventory) to establish that no settlement exists. Pre-existing EFC records (tests.json, external_research_watch, the public Atlas and the CMB page) were read before editing so that older statements are superseded or contradicted explicitly rather than silently overwritten.
